reviewed_by: Claude Code, building the approved held-project banner (Figma page Project hold, 172:2)
reason: Core project holds (#1232) had no interface. A shared ProjectHoldWatch on ApiClient polls the open project's hold (30 s, 5 s while held, refreshed at once when Core refuses work with project_held, stopped on a Core without the route). ProjectHoldNotice shows 'Pausing work in this project' with the grace countdown, then 'Work in this project is paused' with a bordered Release control (icon-only at phone width) behind a confirmation. The composer keeps the draft, disables Send and says when sending works again; the goal panel shows 'paused by update' and hides Resume for goals the hold paused. The assistant contract gains a 'Projects paused for a Core update' section. Selected: new unit suites and the goal panel, runtime notice and chat page suites; the bundled-guidance discovery test; a new real-Core acceptance (area:project-hold, 8 browser projects) that places a hold through Core, checks the banner, disabled Send with kept draft, axe and no horizontal overflow, Keep paused, Release, and Core's released readback; composer-draft-continuity and critical-workspaces mocked areas for composer and workspace layout regressions.
exclusions: No settings destination: a hold is not a setting (documented in the assistant contract). Release uses the pack's CirclePlay icon because the curated icon pack has no unlocked-lock glyph; the approved mockup's lock icon is otherwise matched. area:assistant is not selected: its real-core.spec.ts lanes carry known unrelated rot; the composer change is covered by composer-draft-continuity and the real-Core hold acceptance. tests/test_playwright_impact.py::test_full_manifest_covers_every_product_browser_spec_without_filters fails on unmodified main (ios-shell-real-core.spec.ts) and is not selected. Real-Core acceptance passed locally on model-desktop, model-chromium-320 and model-webkit-390.
